outcome_detail: An executed comparison now exists for Dagu 2.16.6, Prefect 3.8.6 and Temporal through one shared oracle, with per-case pass/fail and setup/operational steps. All three passed stop, retry and checkpoint reuse. SIGKILL under the preregistered protocol and 150 s bound: Temporal passed (15 s, by starting a new worker, with the adapter's 5 s activity heartbeat timeout), Dagu failed (no scheduler: retries refused for the whole bound), Prefect failed (run stayed RUNNING). In a post-hoc variant labelled as a deviation (a Dagu scheduler started after the kill, 270 s window), Dagu recovered in about 182 s (twice: 181.4 s and 182.6 s), still beyond the preregistered bound. The recovery setups were not equivalent: Temporal was given its heartbeat timeout and Dagu (in the variant) its scheduler, but Prefect was not given its documented zombie-flow detection (heartbeats plus an automation), so Prefect's SIGKILL failure reflects this configuration, not Prefect's best available recovery. The observed result does not support excluding Temporal on recovery behaviour; its exclusion now rests on the observed operational burden (a server and worker processes, adapter code for subprocess cancellation, reset-based retry), not on an observed failure. Remaining: Dagster and Restate were not executed, so their exclusion still rests on source review; Prefect's SIGKILL case with zombie-flow detection configured is unexecuted.
limits: One run per engine per scenario for Prefect and Temporal on one WSL2 host; Dagu SIGKILL ran three times (see results). Prefect's zombie-flow detection was not configured (see outcome_detail).

Protocol deviation: the original run's Dagu scheduler (present from the first Dagu debug iteration) and its 270 s window (chosen after cmp-debug-p3 was seen) were not preregistered; labelled late in fix round 1, which also executed the preregistered protocol. The fix-round preregistration was written after the review and is labelled as such.

The Temporal port needs adapter code to stop a subprocess on cancellation (heartbeat-driven); Dagu and Prefect stop step processes natively. Temporal's retry is a history reset that creates a new run id under the same workflow id; the oracle's same_native_run_id is recorded by workflow id and the run ids are listed.

The original run's Dagu scheduler bound its /health server on :8090 on all interfaces for about 3 minutes (and for 30 s in debug iteration cmp-debug-p3, 23:03:05-23:03:35-04:00), departing from the loopback-only rule; fix round 1 disabled it (scheduler.port 0) and verified no listener.

Four development iterations preceded the original reported run (raw/4-6-debug-iterations/); besides harness defects, the SIGKILL window was raised from 30 s to 270 s after cmp-debug-p3's Dagu result was seen (see the deviation result).
No model calls, no broker, no paid API; every started process was stopped.

Unit-level isolation (fix round 2 cross-reference): this receipt's isolation statements cover this gap's own runs only. During fix round 1, between the fix-round preregistration and the F1/F2/F3 reruns, an unquoted heredoc started an unintended `dagu scheduler` (PATH dagu, default config) that wrote state into the default Dagu home $HOME/.local/share/dagu/data and bound :8090 on all interfaces for about 2 min 15 s, and an unintended `codex exec` that was killed while waiting for stdin. Fix round 2 verified that the running host `dagu server` (pid 366, the dagu-equities service) uses DAGU_HOME=$HOME/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/dagu-equities, a different store. See incidents/2026-09-22-fix-round-heredoc-substitution.json.

Resource rule (fix round 3): the Prefect 3.8.6 tree (104 distributions, 207.9 MB installed including run-time __pycache__) was installed with a plain `uv pip install`, not through ecosystem-bounded-run. The installed size is above the 200 MB figure and the tree is large, so the wave's heavy-build rule applied and was not followed; the compressed download was probably smaller, but its size was not recorded. The temporalio tree is 5 distributions, 56.6 MB installed. Both resolved sets are now recorded (resolved_dependency_sets; raw/fix3/venv-*-freeze.txt), so the environments can be rebuilt with `uv pip install -r` of the freeze files.

Helper change after execution (fix round 3): dagu_common.py was edited after this receipt's runs. codex_gate() now raises CodexGateTimeout instead of returning when 2 or more other `codex exec` processes still run at max_wait, and codex_exec_processes() also counts `codex <global options> exec` and the `e` alias. The executed revisions named in this receipt are unchanged and remain the ones that ran. Only one gated model call was made in the whole unit (fix-round F3, gap 2); it waited 0 s with 0 other processes counted by the old matcher, so the timeout path was not reached. Whether the broader matcher would have counted more processes at that time cannot be re-observed. Synthetic test: raw/fix3/codex-gate-test.txt.

resolved_dependency_sets.set_is_the_executed_set: The raw files print three unlabelled epoch lines under a heading that says 'dist-info birth min/max and mtime max (epoch + iso)'; no ISO value is printed. Prefect: 1790131910 on all three lines (2026-09-22T22:51:50-04:00). temporalio: 1790131911 on all three lines (22:51:51-04:00). pyvenv.cfg was born 22:51:49.6 (prefect) and 22:51:50.6 (temporalio). So the dist-info directories were born 22:51:50-22:51:51, the install. The frozen set is the executed set because a reinstall or added package would create a dist-info directory with a later birth, and the newest dist-info birth equals the install time; the comparison started at 23:03 and the first debug iteration at 22:55:13. The separate check headed 'any file in venv modified after newest dist-info birth + 600 s' printed nothing, but its exit status, file filter (whether .pyc was excluded) and a detection control were not recorded, and its 600 s grace window (to about 23:01:51) covers the first debug iterations (cmp-debug-t-1790132113 = 22:55:13). It therefore does not show that no file changed after the install; it adds nothing beyond the dist-info birth argument.
resolved_dependency_sets.download_bytes: Not recorded at install time and not recoverable: the uv cache stores unpacked archives. The installed sizes include __pycache__ written when the engines ran, so they are an upper-bound proxy, not a measured download.
